say: Sixty feet under a wheat field in Montana, two officers sit at the controls for ten nuclear missiles.
Their shift lasts twenty-four hours. The door that seals them in weighs about eight tons.
Problem one: sleep. There's one small bed. One officer can nap. The other must stay awake. Always.
Problem two: food. A cook in the building up top makes your meals, and they ride down the elevator to you.
Problem three: the bathroom. It's right there in the capsule, a few steps from the launch console.
And every few hours, a coded message comes in. You check it, every single time. Because one day, it might be real.
